**The final answer 9 is incorrect.** The correct sum is **138**.

**Reduction.** Write $P(x)=\sum_i c_i (x)_i$ with $(x)_i=x(x-1)\cdots(x-i+1)$ and $c_i\in\mathbb{Z}$. Since $(x)_i=i!\binom{x}{i}$, the condition $p^k\mid P(m)$ for all $m$ holds iff $v_p(c_i)\ge k-v_p(i!)$ for every $i$. The $x^n$-coefficient is $\sum_i c_i\, s(i,n)$, where $s(i,n)$ is the signed Stirling number of the first kind. The coefficient can equal $1$ exactly when some $i\ge n$ has $v_p(i!)\ge k$ and $p\nmid s(i,n)$. Therefore
$$k(n,p)=\max\{\,v_p(i!) : i\ge n,\ p\nmid s(i,n)\,\}.$$

**Mod $p$ structure.** Writing $i=pq+r$ with $0\le r<p$, we have $(x)_i\equiv (x^p-x)^q(x)_r \pmod p$. The lowest-degree term of $(x^p-x)^q(x)_r$ has degree at least $q$, so $p\nmid s(i,n)$ forces $q\le n$.

**Upper bound.** For $p=11$ and $11\le n\le 15$, $v_{11}(i!)=q+[q\ge 11]\le n+1$ when $q\le n$.

**Attained at $i=pn$.** Here $q=n$, $r=0$, and $s(pn,n)\equiv(-1)^n\not\equiv 0\pmod p$, since the only $x^n$ term of $(x^p-x)^n$ is $(-x)^n$. So $k(n,p)=v_p((pn)!)$ in these cases.

- $p=11$: $v_{11}((11n)!)=n+1$, giving $k=12,13,14,15,16$ for $n=11,\dots,15$. Sum $=70$.
- $p=13$: $v_{13}((13n)!)=n+\lfloor n/13\rfloor$, giving $k=11,12,14,15,16$ for $n=11,\dots,15$. Sum $=68$.

I checked the bounds for $p=13$ separately: $q\le n$ and $v_{13}(i!)=q+[q\ge 13]$, so no other $i$ does better.

**Counterexample to the proposed formula.** For $n=11$, $p=11$: $s(121,11)\equiv(-1)^{11}\not\equiv0\pmod{11}$ and $v_{11}(121!)=12$. So $k(11,11)\ge 12$, while the proposed formula gives $1$.

Total: $70+68=138$.

VERDICT: REJECT
